name: Winklepicker shoes

card.summary: Shoes and boots with a very long, sharply pointed toe that elongate the foot line and give outfits a retro, rock-and-roll or goth edge.
card.note: Narrow toe boxes reduce toe room; modern fashion shoes often have shorter toes.

quick.overview:
Winklepickers are shoes or boots with a long, needle-like pointed toe. Wearers use them for a sharp, stylised silhouette and a longer-looking leg line, especially in Teddy Boy, mod, rockabilly, punk and goth styling.

The style dates from the 1950s and has been revived repeatedly since. No studies examine them as a way of looking better; their effect is a visual styling one.
quick.how: People wear them as part of period or subculture outfits, pairing them with slim trousers, such as mod or rockabilly looks. Because the toe is narrow, fit and toe room are the main consideration when choosing a pair.
quick.risks: The narrow, pointed toe box leaves less room for toes than rounder shoes, which can be uncomfortable for some wearers.

lead: Winklepickers are shoes and boots with a very long, sharply pointed toe. The name comes from the English habit of picking winkles (periwinkle snails) out of their shells with a pin.[1] In the United States they were nicknamed 'roach stompers', and in Norway and Sweden 'mosquito chasers'.[1]

The style appeared in the 1950s, inspired by the medieval poulaines worn by European nobility.[1] Women's versions with stiletto heels were popular in the UK in the late 1950s and early 1960s; in the early 1960s the point was often cut off, producing the 'chisel toe'.[1] Sharp-pointed styles returned in the late 1970s and early 1980s, and by the mid-2000s indie bands were wearing them again with mod-inspired clothing.[1]

As a style choice, the long toe extends the visual line of the foot and leg and signals a subculture. They are associated with Teddy Boys, mods, rockers, rockabillies, punks and goths, where they are sometimes called 'pikes'.[1]

chain: Long pointed toe extends the foot line
angle.text: The pointed toe visually lengthens the foot and leg line and finishes slim or period outfits. They are chosen for this distinctive silhouette.

paras: Winklepickers are defined by a toe that tapers to a sharp point, usually extending well past the toes. Shorter variants are described as having a chisel toe.[1] Modern women's shoes generally have shorter toes than the originals, often at the expense of toe room.[1]

The shoe emerged in the 1950s and drew on the long-toed poulaines of medieval European nobility.[1] It was worn by Teddy Boys and later mods; revivals came in the late 1970s and early 1980s and again in the mid-2000s with indie bands.[1]
They remain popular in goth, raggare and rockabilly scenes, and in Germany in modern Vogue goth and punk scenes.[1]
